testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you start moving from a complete stop, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backward when you start moving forward. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, or hitting a shoulder rumble strip.

questions.question: If you notice something while driving that affects safety or could cause mechanical problems, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if the problem goes away.
Include the concerns in your written report.
Try to fix the issue yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Include the concerns in your written report.
questions.explanation: At the end of your driving shift, you may need to fill out a written report about your vehicle's condition. Report anything that could affect safety or cause mechanical problems.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system has very low pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work at all.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system loses pressure. If air pressure gets too low while driving, you should pull over and stop as soon as possible.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car:

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction in any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: On a basic vehicle control skills test, you should be able to:

options.text: Weave between a line of cones.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Water that collects on a roadway can cause:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: Using brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose their stopping power. Do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Also use engine braking.

questions.question: When you are pulled over to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to alert other motorists to your presence.
Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other motorists to your presence.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other motorists to your presence.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers, especially when visibility is poor. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check all of the following about tires, EXCEPT:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: When inspecting tires, check that front tires have at least 4/32 inch tread depth and other tires have at least 2/32 inch tread depth. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, have correct air pressure, and are all the same size.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep the weight of cargo as low as possible.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure may cause a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear fishtails, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: An empty truck:

options.text: Stops in a shorter distance than a full truck.
Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
Stops in the same distance as a full truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances because they have less traction.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
Is not encouraged because it distracts you.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: In cool weather, when temperature rises and ice starts to melt:

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: When ice melts, water sits on top of the ice, making the road more slippery. Always drive slowly and carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Do NOT base your decision to shift gears on:

options.text: The speed shown on your speedometer (mph).
What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Do not shift based on other vehicles.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck:

options.text: Is a good way for new drivers to gain experience.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load with a high center of gravity. The meat swinging affects vehicle handling, so a skilled driver is required.

questions.question: How long must an applicant hold a CLP before taking the skills tests?
questions.explanation: You must hold a Commercial Learner Permit (CLP) for at least 14 days before you can take the skills tests.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake system falls below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before pressure drops below 55 psi. If it does not work during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe if a professional did the repairs.
Are safe if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe. Replace them before driving.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always the right choice.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To stay behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery surfaces like rain or snow. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of aggressive driving?

options.text: Slowing down and keeping a safe distance from other vehicles.
Making hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making hand gestures that anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving. Be realistic about travel time, allow for delays, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and do not make hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to keep space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: Yes, it gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
Only if you are driving with a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle for safe driving. This gives you time to act if a problem occurs.

questions.question: What part prevents air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks?
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor.
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes do not work instantly. Air takes time to travel through the lines to reach the brakes. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, how much following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller ones.

questions.question: What should you do if you hear or feel something unusual while driving?

options.text: Hope the vehicle is okay until another driver takes over.
Check it to find out what the problem is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it to find out what the problem is.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked right away.

questions.question: How should cargo in a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured so it does not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured so it does not move.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be secured properly to keep it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid a hazard, should you brake?

options.text: No, braking can cause the wheels to lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, braking can cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning sharply to avoid a hazard. Braking can cause your wheels to lock and make your vehicle skid out of control.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valve markings usually say:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes (made before 1975) have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you need to back up, you should:

options.text: Get out and walk around to see what's there.
Avoid using both side mirrors because it's distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can watch them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to see what's there.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and look at your path. Check that you have enough space on the sides and overhead.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Unbalanced cargo makes a vehicle hard to control. Balance your cargo weight carefully when loading.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable. It swings during travel and its center of gravity is high.

questions.question: What is the left lane rule?

options.text: Heavy vehicles must only drive in the left lane on a three-lane road.
Heavy vehicles can only use the left lane on a three-lane road to make a left turn.
Heavy vehicles can never use the left lane on a three-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy vehicles can only use the left lane on a three-lane road to make a left turn.
questions.explanation: In Washington State, vehicles or combinations over 10,000 pounds cannot drive in the left lane of a limited-access road with three or more lanes in one direction, unless turning left.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, the parking brake is used by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: Newer vehicles with air brakes use a yellow, diamond-shaped knob for the parking brake. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before starting a trip:

options.text: They will get clean after driving a short distance.

questions.explanation: During your pre-trip check, clean the mirrors and windshield if they are dirty. Anything blocking your view is unsafe.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle on any uphill grade. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: When accelerating on a wet road or other slippery surface, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is on only one axle, you will still have more control when braking than you would without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are hazardous because:

options.text: Drivers hurrying to leave may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers hurrying to leave may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may pull into traffic quickly without warning or step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
Protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board protects a driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not respond to angry gestures from other drivers. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on rear tires.
Are safe to use if carrying light loads.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include distance traveled, fuel purchased, trip origin, destination, and the Vehicle Identification Number. It does not need meal information.

questions.question: A vehicle loaded with dirt or sand must be covered if:

options.text: Less than six inches of space remain between the load and the top of the truck bed.
The driver has had their license for less than one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less than six inches of space remain between the load and the top of the truck bed.
questions.explanation: In Washington State, dirt, sand, or gravel loads must be covered if there is less than six inches of space between the load and the top of the truck bed.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.
